\section{Results}\label{sec:results}

\subsection{Where knowledge pays: the twin's map}\label{sec:res-twin}
% Numbers: docs/results_twin_v4.md (generated by src.analysis.twin_report from results/v4/twin_map,
% 240 worlds per protocol) and paper/tools/fig_twin_map.py; to move into generated macros.
% The slices and RQ2 (kernel version 13) are added when pulled.

No cell of the grid pays, under either protocol (\cref{fig:twin-map}). The graph's accuracy gain
over distance routing stays within a few thousandths of a log unit: the cell medians of
$\log(\mathrm{RMSE}_D / \mathrm{RMSE}_C)$ range from $-0.012$ to $+0.009$ under early stopping and
from $-0.025$ to $-0.002$ under converged pooling, and every cell's 97.5\,\% quantile is above zero.
This is not because the graph is too wrong. Even the oracle, which routes the true pumping, gains
only about 2 to 8\,\% of RMSE over distance routing ($\log(\mathrm{RMSE}_T / \mathrm{RMSE}_C)$ between
$-0.021$ and $-0.086$). Where pumping carries \SI{30}{\percent} of the head's training variance and its weekly
timing follows the weather, knowing which facilities reach a well can improve the simulated head only a
little. A real-data D versus C contrast without a detected gain is therefore the expected outcome
in the four cells that bracket the real graph, not evidence that the graph is wrong.

The graph matters more for the reasons than for the accuracy, but only under one protocol. Under
converged pooling, arm~D recovers the pumping contribution better than arm~C in 65 to 95\,\% of the
worlds of a cell (82\,\% on average over cells); under early stopping, in only 15 to 35\,\% (25\,\%).
One reading is that early stopping halts the fit before the model separates pumping from the
seasonal weather that moves with it, so the routing hardly matters, while converged pooling lets
the routing decide how the head's summer decline is shared between the drivers. In absolute terms, early stopping recovers arm~D's
pumping better in 8 of the 12 cells and simulates the drought slightly better (median drought
efficiency $+0.03$). This motivates pairing the protocols rather than choosing one: early
stopping for the accuracy contrasts and converged pooling for the explanation claims, declared
before the real-data runs. % pending Gate 3 point 1 In the base grid no world has wrong reasons for either arm (score~6: 0 of 240
per protocol), as expected where the generator lies inside the model's class; the slices with an
omitted driver and responses the model does not have are where wrong reasons can appear.

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{figures/twin_map}
\caption{The twin's knowledge-value map. Each cell summarises 20 semi-synthetic worlds with a share
$\varepsilon$ of false pumping links in the graph and a share $u$ of the true pumping that the graph
misses; rows are the two fitting protocols. Left and middle: median log ratio of the drought RMSE
of the graph arm (D) and of the oracle (T) to the distance arm (C); negative values favour D or T.
Right: share of worlds in which D recovers the pumping contribution with a lower error than C. A
cell that pays would be outlined; none does.}
\label{fig:twin-map}
\end{figure}
